rationale: HSA1 — A DEPENDENCY THE MODULE DOES NOT DECLARE IS A CLAIM, NOT SILENCE. The haskell wall was 60,898 ambiguous/unresolved of 193,418 edges, and its two largest classes are the two dependencies the language spells as a BARE UPPER-CASE name: the type class in an `instance` head and the data constructor in an expression. MEASURED over the whole admitted population (3,702 files / 6 repos): implements 11,563 unresolved, led by Show 2,459 / Eq 1,899 / Generic 1,404 / Ord 703 / ToJSON 662 / FromJSON 641 / NFData 530 / Hashable 327; instantiates 10,978 unresolved, led by Just 3,657 / Right 1,017 / Left 617. None can be declared by a corpus file that does not already declare it, so every row was a dependency published with NO reading. The claim is the fleet's `externalTarget`, and it is SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by care: the arbiter consults a claim only where the name model has nothing (`decls === 0`), so a name the project really declares keeps its resolved/ambiguous answer and this row can never refute it. MEASURED EFFECT: wall 60,898 -> 43,364, verified external 9,988 -> 27,522, refuted 0, ambiguous unchanged at 9,326. The twins are the boundary: a class declared in THIS module must not be claimed, and neither must the module's own constructor — which is why the candidate set carries CONSTRUCTORS separately from types.

expectRelationships.comment: THE POSITIVE ROW. `Show` is `base`'s class; this module declares nothing of that spelling, so the row says so — and the arbiter verifies it by finding nothing. Before this rule the row was one of 11,563 unresolved `implements` edges that named a library class and said nothing about it.

THE LOCAL TWIN. `class Shape` is declared above in this module, so `instance Shape Bool` is a project-internal dependency; the claim must not appear, or the row would assert that the project does not declare a class it declares eight lines earlier.

THE BUILTIN CONSTRUCTOR. `Just` belongs to `Maybe`, which the language supplies; 3,657 population rows named it with no reading. The claim is about the NAME, and the arbiter consults it only where the project declares nothing.

THE CONSTRUCTOR TWIN IN THE SAME EXPRESSION. `MkFoo` is this module's own constructor of `data Foo`, so `Just (MkFoo 1)` must claim one half of the row and not the other — the guard is the declaration table, and it needs CONSTRUCTORS in that table: the first version of this rule claimed `MkFoo` because only the TYPE name `Foo` was collected, and this fixture is what caught it.
second builtin, so a fix that special-cased `Just` cannot pass
third builtin — the `Either` pair is claimed in both directions
THE LOCAL CONSTRUCTOR, ALONE. Same name as the twin above, no claim either time.

forbidRelationships.comment: THE FALSE-CLAIM NEGATIVE. Claiming a class this module declares is exactly the defect the guard exists for.
second false-claim negative, on the constructor half — the one the fixture caught in the first cut.
THE SILENCE NEGATIVE. Without the claim `Show` falls back to the wall it came from; this row makes that revert red.
